key_insight: Physics-guided deep learning recovers 3D bubble positions and physical-equivalent diameters from single-camera shadowgraphs, addressing size–defocus ambiguity without stereoscopic hardware.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a scalable diagnostic for dense bubbly flows while reducing optical-access, calibration, and hardware demands.
method: Render DNS-resolved bubbles using validated Monte Carlo ray tracing at multiple focal-plane settings.
Preprocess images into bubble crops and split training and evaluation data by DNS timestamp to prevent leakage.
Predict signed depth and diameter with a multitask network conditioned on focal-plane coordinates.
evidence_signal: Using 900 frames and 87,728 labeled instances, the study reports ~97.6% normalized depth accuracy on held-out data, <9.71% diameter error in a 180-bubble closed-loop test, and 68–92% experimental diameter-PDF overlap.
watch_item: Reconstruction errors increase with distance from the focal plane, defining a recoverability limit that must guide deployment.
paper_title: Monocular 3D bubble reconstruction: DNS-informed ray tracing and deep learning
